SpaceX doesn't just know how to recover rockets in space — it also knows how to place orders to acquire AI companies. In February this year, Starlink's parent company brought xAI (which includes X, formerly known as Twitter) under its umbrella. In April this year, SpaceX signed a cooperation agreement with Cursor, a competitor to Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. As of August 14, the acquisition has been completed. The company, renamed SpaceXAI, has also recently launched the Grok Bot and Grok 4.6 model with Cursor's assistance.

Updated August 14, 2026: SpaceXAI has completed the acquisition of Cursor.

Updated June 16, 2026: SpaceX acquired Cursor one week after becoming a publicly listed company.

The original report has been updated as follows:

SpaceX struck a $10 billion deal with Cursor ahead of its $60 billion acquisition

Cursor, popular among software engineers who use Macs paired with AI for coding, was one of the first services to connect large language model AI to the application development workflow.

In April this year, the two companies stated that SpaceX and Cursor were "working closely together, committed to creating the world's top programming and knowledge-work AI."

The original partnership included SpaceX paying Cursor $1 billion:

Cursor further disclosed details of the partnership in April this year, before the acquisition was completed:

Cursor is partnering with SpaceX to accelerate our model training work. Composer, released less than half a year ago, is our first agentic coding model. Subsequently, Composer 1.5 scaled up reinforcement learning by more than 20 times. Composer 2 then added continual pre-training techniques, achieving frontier-level performance at a fraction of the cost of other models. With every step up in compute, model capabilities improve significantly. We have always wanted to take our training work to the next level, but compute has been the bottleneck. This partnership allows our team to leverage xAI's Colossus infrastructure, substantially enhancing the intelligence of our models.

The partnership between SpaceX and Cursor has strengthened the ranks of competitors to Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI Codex agentic coding software.
